conviction_note: Q3 was pre-released on 2026-11-03 at the top of guidance and the stock rose 4.5% that day, so the quarter is mostly priced. The print turns on the first explicit Q4 guide: the FY2026 range of $734-742m less the $536.7m year to date implies Q4 revenue of $197.3-205.3m, or +11-16% against $177.2m, after Q3 grew 20%. The CFO has signalled 'typical prudence'. Against that, Opera beat its implied Q4 by 7-9% last year, the stock is down 12.5% in 20 days, and calls are bid. The findings sum to -0.6 and the scaled number is -0.12, with p_up 49 on a 6% abs move. The two agree in sign and both are near zero; the evidence does not settle the direction of the guide.
bar: Q3 revenue consensus $181.8m and EPS $0.35 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-10, https://finviz.com/news/420440/opera-must-prove-its-guided-slowdown-is-conservative-as-shares-slide-toward-range-lows). Company guide: Q3 revenue $181-183m and adj. EBITDA $41-43m; FY2026 revenue $734-742m and adj. EBITDA $172-175m (Q2 release 2026-08-19, https://www.webull.com/news/15429157784929280). FY consensus is about $738m (same EW preview), which implies a Q4 consensus near $201m. Q3 actuals were pre-released 2026-11-03: revenue $182.8m and adj. EBITDA $43.2m (https://finviz.com/news/414169/opera-announces-strong-user-trajectory-and-q3-results-at-the-top-end-of-guidance). The revenue bar rests on a company guide plus one estimate source. The EPS bar has one source and an unclear measure (IFRS or adjusted), so every EPS finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 1.6M ADS at the FINRA 2026-06-30 settlement, 4.46 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/opra/short-interest, page updated 2026-07-14). No November settlement was found. Opera's free float is small, so this is moderate rather than crowded. Baseline 25-delta skew is -15.57 vol points (calls bid over puts, 'upside paid'). But the ATM spread is 104% of mid, so the chain is barely usable. Put/call OI ratio 1.54. ATM IV is 103% at 4 days to expiry against 62% realised 20-day vol; that implies an event move of roughly 9-11%, with the wide-spread caveat. Run-up is -12.5% over 20 days, -0.4% over 5 days, and -24.9% from the 52-week high. EW puts spot $15.49 against a 200-day average of $17.10 and a post-earnings low of $14.50. EW says sentiment is mildly bearish and the guided slowdown and the Google renewal risk are already discounted.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was pre-released on 2026-11-03, two weeks before this print. Revenue was $182.8m (+20% YoY), at the top of the $181-183m guide and $1.0m (+0.5%) above the $181.8m consensus. Adj. EBITDA was $43.2m, above the $41-43m guide. Desktop MAU reached 100m in October (+16% YoY). The beat over the top of the guide has shrunk each quarter: Q1 was $3.8m above the top, Q2 $0.1m above, and Q3 inside the range. Ad growth slowed from +27% in Q2 to +22%, and query growth from +21% to +17%. So the reported quarter carries almost no new information on 11-17.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The pre-release day (2026-11-03) moved +4.46% in the baseline's 6-K row, so the market has already traded these numbers. Q2 2026 beat above the top of its range and the stock fell 7.12% (2026-08-19). Q1 2026 beat the top by $3.8m and rose 5.32%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. That is the point of filing it: a full release that repeats $182.8m and $43.2m adds nothing. If it were not priced, the Nov 3 session would not show a +4.5% move and the 11-10 EW preview would still carry the pre-release consensus. It does carry the old EPS figure (see the EPS finding).
findings.independence: Same figures in Benzinga's 2026-11-03 copy (https://www.webull.com/news/15859992570258432) and Panabee (https://www.panabee.com/news/opera-earnings-q3-2026). Both repeat the same company release, so this is one document.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide is the swing factor, and the company has signalled caution. The FY2026 guide of $734-742m (raised 2026-08-19) less the year to date (Q1 $175.8m, Q2 $178.1m, Q3 $182.8m = $536.7m) implies Q4 revenue of $197.3-205.3m. That is +11-16% against Q4 2025's $177.2m, after +20% in Q3. FY consensus of about $738m implies a Q4 near $201m (+13.5%). On 2026-11-03 the CFO said the company will 'approach our final Q4 guidance with our typical prudence' and that 'our reporting timeline allows us to carefully assess trends'. Results come out 19 days later than last year (2025-10-29 vs 2026-11-17), so the guide will be set with about seven weeks of Q4 data in hand. In August the CFO said Q4 is built on 'a more normalized Q4 spike' than the extraordinary spikes of 2024 and 2025. Against this, Opera beat its implied Q4 2025 guide of about $162-165m with $177.2m (+7-9%). Expected outcome: a guide that leaves FY at roughly $735-743m, close to consensus, with a small risk that 'prudence' means a Q4 range centred below $201m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A raised FY guide with a Q3 range above consensus was sold -7.12% on 2026-08-19. The FY2026 first guide with a Q4 2025 beat bought +23.38% on 2026-02-26. A raised guide bought +5.32% on 2026-04-28. The Q3 2025 raise on 2025-10-29 was reportedly followed by a fall (snippet: 'down 9.0% after raising 2025 guidance', simplywall.st, close not confirmed). Guide moves on this name run about 5-23 points either way.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. EW says 'the guided slowdown' is discounted, and the stock is at range lows with calls bid. What is not public is the Q4 range itself. If the market expected a cut, the skew would be put-bid rather than -15.6, and FY consensus would sit below the $734-742m midpoint rather than at about $738m.
findings.independence: The implied Q4 comes from the 2026-08-19 FY guide (https://www.webull.com/news/15429157784929280), the Q1 release (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1555776/opera-reports-first-quarter-2026-results-with-both-revenue-and-adjusted-ebitda-exceeding-high-end-of-guidance-ranges) and the Q4 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1737450/000119312526073367/opra-ex99_1.htm). The 'normalized Q4 spike' quote is from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15429727749776384). The Q4 2025 beat of its implied guide uses the FY2025 guide of $600-603m (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/35756004/opera-reports-third-quarter-2025-results-ahead-of-expectations-raises-full-year-guidance-ranges-for-both-revenue-and-adjusted-ebitda) against $614.8m actual. Each source points a different way on sign.

findings.finding: There is a possible headline EPS miss against a stale bar. The 2026-11-03 pre-release puts Q3 IFRS net income at $27.6m. That includes a $3.3m impairment reversal and excludes $6.9m of SBC. Q2's $27.6m net income gave diluted EPS of $0.30. So Q3 IFRS EPS should be about $0.30-0.31, against an EW consensus of $0.35 that was still posted on 2026-11-10, after the pre-release. On an adjusted basis (adding back SBC, removing the reversal) it would be about $0.34-0.35, in line. Which measure the wire compares against is unclear.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-19 the drop of -5.5% pre-market and -7.12% on the day was attributed to an adj. EPS of $0.26 against $0.27 consensus, despite a revenue beat and a raised guide (https://finviz.com/news/383706/opera-shares-drop-despite-revenue-beat-and-stronger-2026-outlook).
findings.why_not_priced: Net income has been public since 11-03, so a careful reader has it. But a published $0.35 consensus a week after the pre-release suggests the EPS bar was not reset, and on this name a one-cent EPS miss drew the wire headline last quarter. If the bar were current, EW's $0.35 would have moved to the low $0.30s.
findings.independence: The net income figure comes from the pre-release (https://finviz.com/news/414169/opera-announces-strong-user-trajectory-and-q3-results-at-the-top-end-of-guidance), and the Q2 EPS per share from https://www.webull.com/news/15429157784929280. The bar has one source and an unclear measure, so this is capped small.

findings.finding: OPay's IPO was pulled. OPay priced its NYSE IPO at $19, the bottom of the $19-21 range (about $4B valuation, $304m raise), on 2026-10-30. It then withdrew before trading, citing an unnamed foreign regulatory inquiry it called immaterial. Pre-pull indications were $16.25-16.75, roughly $3.4-3.5B. Opera holds about 9.5% of OPay, carried at $300.9m at Q2. That is about 22% of Opera's roughly $1.37B market cap (88.9M ADS x $15.43). The 11-17 release and call are Opera's first chance to give the Q3 fair value and an update.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on OPay. The pull came in the same 20-day window in which OPRA fell 12.5% (Nasdaq 100 -3.5% on 10-30 itself), so the stock has already absorbed some of it.
findings.why_not_priced: The pull itself is priced (2026-10-30). What is not: whether Opera marks the stake at Sept 30 near the $19 pricing (about $330-380m, a write-up) or holds it, and anything management says about the inquiry. A mark near $19 is a small positive on a stake worth a fifth of market cap. Silence or a cautious tone leaves the overhang. It probably goes through OCI rather than adj. EBITDA, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Separate reports: American Banker 2026-11-03 (https://www.americanbanker.com/news/o-no-african-fintech-opay-pulls-u-s-ipo-at-last-minute), Nairametrics 2026-10-31 on the indicated open (https://nairametrics.com/2026/10/31/why-opay-ipo-sale-was-halted-after-debut-on-nyse/), and the stake size and carrying value (https://launchbaseafrica.com/2026/04/24/an-85-chance-of-a-3-1bn-ipo-within-two-years-inside-operas-high-stakes-opay-bet/; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002103076/000119312526418812/d56487df1.htm F-1). The sign is genuinely two-way.

findings.finding: The Google search agreement (query revenue is about 35% of revenue, $62.1m in Q2) runs under the Dec 2025 Mehta remedy, which caps default-search contracts at one year. On the Q1 call management said it had renewed 'for the year due to DOJ requirements', expected 'no surprises', and said renewal talks happen in H2. EW lists the unresolved H2 renewal as a bear-case factor already discounted. A renewal confirmed on the 11-17 call would remove it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no print in the window where the Google deal was the headline. The 2024 extension was announced separately (https://WWW.INVESTING.COM/news/company-news/opera-secures-google-search-deal-extension-through-2025-93CH-3364652).
findings.why_not_priced: EW says the risk is discounted. A renewal announcement would be new; I found no 2026 renewal release. If the market had priced a clean renewal, the stock would not sit at range lows with EW naming the renewal as the bear case. If it had priced a loss, query revenue would not be guided to keep growing.
findings.independence: The one-year remedy is in https://searchengineland.com/judge-limits-google-default-search-deals-one-year-465863. EW's bear-case framing is at https://finviz.com/news/420440/opera-must-prove-its-guided-slowdown-is-conservative-as-shares-slide-toward-range-lows. Q3 query growth of +17% (pre-release) shows no disruption so far.

findings.finding: Opera has room to buy back more. Under the $300m two-year buyback approved in Feb 2026, cumulative repurchases through 2026-06-30 were only 1.78M shares for $28.1m (average $15.79), with Q2 buying at an average of $17.44. Spot is $15.43. FCF runs at about 60-85% of adj. EBITDA (about $43m a quarter). The Q3 release will disclose Q3 buybacks, and with the stock 25% off its high, an acceleration or a 10b5-1 statement is plausible. The semi-annual $0.40 dividend has historically been declared separately (6-Ks in December and June), so it is not expected in this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Feb 2026 print that announced the $300m program bought +23.38%, but that day also carried the first FY guide and a Q4 beat, so the buyback's share of the move cannot be separated.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 repurchase volume is not public. If heavy buying were assumed, the stock would not be trading below the Q2 average buyback price. Sized small because the program is known and $272m remains.
findings.independence: Program size from the Q4 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1737450/000119312526073367/opra-ex99_1.htm). FCF conversion from the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15429727749776384).

findings.finding: This is a proxy for e-commerce ad demand into Q4. Opera's ad growth is 'led by E Commerce' (Q2 call). Ad growth slowed from 27% in Q2 to 22% in Q3. The EU's flat €3 per-item parcel duty took effect 2026-07-01, and by late June Temu's share of European Google Shopping auctions had roughly halved since March while Shein's fell toward zero. Sensor Tower data also shows Temu cut US ad spend on most platforms through May 2026. If Opera's e-commerce advertisers include these platforms, Q4 holiday ad demand could be softer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print was attributed to advertiser concentration. Ad revenue is about 65% of the total.
findings.why_not_priced: Opera has never named its advertiser concentration, so the market cannot map this. But Q3 already absorbed the fee (ads still +22%), and AliExpress increased its Google Shopping presence over the same period. This is macro-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The company's own Q3 ad decel (27% to 22%) is in the 11-03 pre-release (https://finviz.com/news/414169/opera-announces-strong-user-trajectory-and-q3-results-at-the-top-end-of-guidance). Temu US cuts: https://www.ecomcrew.com/temu-cut-u-s-ad-spend-by-up-to-95-on-most-platforms-but-its-user-base-held-steady/. The broader series (Opera ads +22%) says the effect is modest.

outside_window.finding: An OPay IPO relaunch after the inquiry concludes (OPay says it is 'confident that the inquiry will be concluded satisfactorily in the near future'). A completed listing would give Opera's ~9.5% stake a market price. No date is announced.
The next $0.40 semi-annual dividend declaration has historically come in a separate December 6-K (2025-12-11 row in the baseline).

baseline_tension: The skew (calls bid, -15.6) and the -12.5% 20-day slide to range lows say downside is already taken. My small net negative rests on the CFO's 'prudence' cue and slowing growth, so it cuts mildly against the skew. That moved p_up from 48 to 49, and the Q4 guide finding from -0.5 to -0.3. The chain's 104% spread makes the skew weak evidence.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (positioning): the negative Q4-guide finding sits against an upside-paid skew and a -12.5% run-up, so it shrank from -0.5 to -0.3 and p_up moved from 48 to 49.
Rule 5 (a proxy loses to a broad series): the Temu/Shein/EU parcel proxy shrank from -0.3 to -0.2, because Opera's own Q3 ad growth (+22%) already absorbed the July fee.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): the EPS finding was already capped at -0.5 for its single, ambiguous source; left unchanged.

The rule on FPI reaction histories: the base rate was rebuilt from the 3 confirmed earnings 6-Ks (median |move| about 7.1). abs_move stays at 6.0 because the quarter was pre-released (lowering it) and a first explicit Q4 guide is due (raising it).
Rule 8 (thin coverage) left unchanged: no confirmed unpriced company number was found, so nothing was enlarged.
